quote: Recent papers (as well as multiple github projects) have made use of a restricted version of this, restricting generation from the language model to only extend the current prefix in ways that are grammatical under an unweighted CFG; then only grammatical text or code will be generated.

It can be attractively extended to compute the probabilities of the possible next words . This is a standard way to compute autoregressive language model probabilities under a PCFG to support cognitive modeling  and speech recognition . Such probabilities could further be combined with those of a large autoregressive language model to form a product-of-experts model. Recent papers (as well as multiple github projects) have made use of a restricted version of this, restricting generation from the language model to only extend the current prefix in ways that are grammatical under an unweighted CFG; then only grammatical text or code will be generated .
